request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The audit now writes the rollup lines, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **`Rollups`** (new file `rollup/Rollups.java`) works out the sheet's figures on the server: each person's claimed and due-total, plus the sheet's two totals. It reuses the existing `Dues.total`, so the numbers match what the screen shows, including `n/a`.
- **Before and after each change:** every endpoint that changes data now reads the figures just before saving. After the change's own audit line, it compares them with the figures afterwards. Those endpoints are add/edit person, add/edit claim, claim status change, set rate, statement, and set today.
- **What gets written:**
  - one `ROLLUP sheet=… by=… person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…` line for each person whose figures moved, in the order people were added. A newly added person always gets a line.
  - then a `TOTALS … claimed-total=… due-total=…` line, only if a sheet total changed.
  - nothing at all when no figure moved.

**Differences from the request's wording**
- The request writes `ROLLUP name=<name>`, but the spec expects `person=<name>`. I followed the spec.
- The sheet's due-total leaves out people whose due-total is `n/a`, as the screen already does. So a sheet can show `due-total=0.00` while a person shows `n/a`, which is what the spec expects.

**Other changes**
- `ValidateToday` now also passes on the today request, so the today step can record who made the change. Its own behaviour hasn't changed and it still writes no audit line of its own.
- The extra steps are wired in the endpoint YAML files under `officefloor/rest/api/sheets/`.
- Nothing changed in the database schema or the front end.
